articles.title: Community Day invites local hosts to bring the open home together
articles.dek: Meetup registration opens for November 7, with a host playbook, event map and an October 5 deadline for merchandise requests.
body: People who want to bring their local open-home community together can register a meetup for November 7. Open Home Foundation Community Day welcomes gatherings around Home Assistant, ESPHome and Music Assistant, with a new website that puts local events on a shared map.

Missy Quarry’s announcement turns August’s save-the-date into practical help for hosts. She and event organizer Florencia have prepared a Community Meetups Playbook covering venues, activities, reimbursement and guests’ privacy in photographs. Hosts can add their event to the Luma calendar and create an invitation image with the supplied asset generator.

Official merchandise requests close on October 5. The foundation also offers reimbursement for eligible event expenses and locally produced merchandise under its guidelines, with requests due by December 7; purchases from its own store are excluded. The host resources and calendar give organizers a place to start planning while guests look for a gathering nearby.

articles.title: Home Assistant keeps busy dashboards from exhausting memory
articles.dek: Suggested controls avoid loading a month of detailed activity at once on homes with heavy automation use.
body: Opening the Home dashboard can bring down Home Assistant in homes that generate large numbers of actions through scripts or external automation tools. Its suggested-controls calculation reads a month of activity at once, potentially allocating gigabytes and exhausting the system’s memory.

Paulus Schoutsen changes the calculation to read and count records in batches. It keeps the same suggestions while avoiding the large allocation that could make every attempt to reopen the dashboard fail again.

articles.title: Music Assistant separates private music accounts from shared sources
articles.dek: Account ownership and access settings prepare more personal listening in households with several members.
body: Music Assistant’s server gains a way to keep personal music accounts separate from those shared around the house. Each source has an owner and access settings for private use, selected people, all members or guests. Search, browsing and playback respect those choices, and playback prefers the listener’s own account.

Marcel van der Veldt’s work preserves existing access when converting older settings. It also prepares members to connect and manage their own accounts, although that self-management still needs role permissions and the companion interface. Administrators remain responsible for changing access in the server implementation.

articles.title: Home Assistant keeps device parts beside the equipment they belong to
articles.dek: Dashboard and automation pickers distinguish identically named outlets, while generated entity names gain the parent device.
body: Two devices called “Outlet 1” are easier to tell apart when each appears beneath its own power strip. Home Assistant nests device parts beneath their parent in the dashboard card editor, automation target picker and target details; parts without their own area follow the parent’s room.

The same relationship joins the default format for generated entity IDs, between the area and device name. Together, the changes keep the equipment that gives an outlet or other device part its context visible when people choose a target or identify it by name.

articles.title: Hikvision alerts tell Home Assistant what crossed the camera
articles.dek: Smart detections carry people, vehicle and supported pet classifications, while lost camera connections stop leaving stale motion states.
body: Hikvision camera owners gain a direct way to build Home Assistant automations around what a camera detected. Motion, line-crossing and field-detection events carry human, vehicle or supported pet classifications, so a notification can distinguish a person from passing traffic without reading the camera’s raw event feed.

Paul Tarjan also makes the existing binary sensors show unavailable when the camera’s event stream disconnects. A camera that goes offline during motion no longer leaves an indefinitely active sensor behind. Devices or events without a classification still report a generic detection.

articles.title: Home Assistant keeps ESPHome devices connected through startup trouble
articles.dek: A failed dashboard check no longer disables the entire integration until Home Assistant restarts.
body: Home Assistant keeps its ESPHome integration running when Supervisor is temporarily unreachable during startup. Previously, a failed check for the ESPHome dashboard app could take down the entire integration even though the device connections did not need Supervisor.

The change restores the saved dashboard information and skips the installation check when Supervisor is not ready. This avoids leaving every ESPHome device unavailable after Supervisor itself recovers, a state that previously required restarting Home Assistant.

articles.title: ESPHome keeps building firmware after the dialog closes
articles.dek: Device Builder carries the job into its background queue and keeps the finished download within reach.
body: Closing ESPHome's installation dialog no longer cancels a firmware build in progress. Using the close button, Escape or the surrounding backdrop sends the job to the background queue; the Stop button remains the way to cancel it.

The Firmware tasks view keeps the finished download within reach, including after a failed job is retried there. The change lets makers move on in Device Builder without losing the build they started.

articles.title: Home Assistant lets mowers stop without heading home
articles.dek: A distinct stop command cancels mowing, with an idle state and matching controls for MQTT-connected mowers.
body: A mower needs a way to end its current job without immediately returning to its dock. Home Assistant adds a stop action for that purpose, separate from pause, which preserves a task for resuming, and dock, which sends the mower home.

Paul Bottein carries the change through mower controls and support for MQTT-connected models. A new idle state describes a mower that is stopped but neither paused nor docked. The official developer announcement identifies Core 2026.10 for the capability; each mower integration must support the action.

articles.title: Music Assistant keeps Linux listening sessions awake
articles.dek: The desktop app prevents automatic sleep during playback and fixes blank windows on affected Wayland desktops.
body: Music Assistant’s Linux desktop app prevents automatic sleep, screen blanking and automatic locking while music plays, then releases the restriction when playback pauses. A deliberate suspend still works; the KDE fallback prevents blanking and locking but cannot prevent suspend.

Cindi adds those controls, while Peter Grace fixes blank Flatpak windows on affected Wayland desktops. Both make verified first contributions to the desktop-app repository, with David Bishop following up on playback controls and display detection.

articles.title: Bitvis Power Hub brings smart-meter readings into Home Assistant
articles.dek: The new integration discovers the meter reader locally and creates sensors for the measurements a meter actually supplies.
body: Bitvis Power Hub owners gain a Home Assistant integration for the reader connected to their smart meter’s home-network port. It listens to the Power Hub’s local network broadcasts for power, energy, voltage and current measurements, creating per-phase or total sensors only when those readings are supplied.

Setup discovers the reader automatically or accepts its IP address, checking that data arrives before adding it. MandusBorjesson makes their first contribution to Home Assistant Core with the integration.

articles.title: Home Assistant Cloud guidance removes a misleading network test
articles.dek: Revised troubleshooting explains a host network reset and why Thread and Matter users must restore IPv6 afterward.
body: Home Assistant Cloud troubleshooting no longer sends people past a working fix because their browser passes an IPv6 test. Nabu Casa’s revised guidance explains that the browser can test a different machine and network route from the Home Assistant host, where stale addresses can still block sign-in or remote access.

Ashton rewrites the steps as a reset: temporarily disable IPv6, restart the host, sign in and restore the setting. The guidance explicitly tells Thread and Matter users to put IPv6 back, and explains that an immediate return of the problem points to an unresolved network fault.

body: Silla Prism and Besen charger owners gain controls alongside their readings in Home Assistant. Ermanno Baschiera adds a Silla Prism selector for Solar, Normal and Pause, advancing an integration whose first version exposed readings without these controls.

For Besen, moryoav adds a charging-current setting using the charger’s reported maximum. Silla’s own load-balancing pause remains distinct from the selectable Pause mode: it shows as unknown in the mode selector while the existing status sensor continues to describe the port.

articles.title: Home Assistant accepts connections started by ESPHome devices
articles.dek: The integration gains another route back to a known device when it cannot open the connection itself.
body: Home Assistant gains another route to an ESPHome device when it cannot open the usual connection: it accepts a connection started by the device instead. The integration and ESPHome client library recognize the incoming session through the device’s existing encryption key.

J. Nick Koston’s work still requires the device to be reachable for its initial setup in Home Assistant. It refuses unknown devices and entries without encryption keys, and needs device firmware that supports outgoing connections. The Home Assistant side adds no setting to manage.

articles.title: Assist stops adding duplicate shopping-list items
articles.dek: Repeated voice requests reuse an existing item or bring a checked-off item back onto the list.
body: Asking Assist to add something already on the Home Assistant Shopping List no longer creates another copy. A matching unchecked item is reused, while a checked-off item is reactivated for the next shop.
The correction applies to additions through Assist and voice intents. The Shopping List’s direct add actions keep their existing behavior.

articles.title: Matter.js detects Bluetooth proxies that lose power
articles.dek: The server releases stale device connections within 45 to 60 seconds instead of waiting for another command.
body: A Bluetooth proxy that lost power could leave Matter.js Server believing it was still connected, keeping the devices it had reported assigned to a connection that no longer worked. The server checks for a response every 15 seconds and removes an unresponsive proxy within 45 to 60 seconds.

Ingo Fischer’s correction also prevents a delayed response from reviving a connection after setup has timed out. This is Matter.js Server connection cleanup; updating the list of devices offered for Matter setup needs separate work.

articles.title: Home Assistant’s Android app recovers an interrupted dashboard load
articles.dek: Returning after the app was paused mid-load no longer produces a connection error for a reachable server.
body: Home Assistant’s Android app restarts a dashboard load when the app resumes before the original connection finished. Previously, putting the app in the background while it was loading could leave it stuck until a ten-second timeout displayed a connection error, even though the server was reachable.
The same correction restores the page reload after Improv setup on older Home Assistant versions, where a missing reload could leave a blank screen.

articles.title: Roborock wet-and-dry vacuums report changes without the minute-long wait
articles.dek: Device updates show cleaning and docking promptly, with polling retained for readings the vacuum does not send.
body: Home Assistant follows the updates sent by Roborock wet-and-dry vacuums when a clean starts or the machine returns to its dock. Those changes previously waited for the next one-minute poll.

Polling remains a fallback for measurements the device does not send itself. A failed poll no longer marks a vacuum unavailable while its own updates are still arriving, and readings stay unknown until the device has supplied them.

articles.title: Music Assistant breaks an Endless Mix out of repetition
articles.dek: Mixes started from one song explore related tracks instead of cycling through the same small pool.
body: An Endless Mix started from one song could keep returning to the same handful of tracks. Music Assistant changes how it finds the next batch: it follows several steps through related songs, taking a different path each time while staying connected to the starting track.

The fix addresses services that return the same recommendations for the same song, reported with Navidrome and AudioMuse. It also applies to autoplay and music-quiz pools started from one track; mixes based on an artist, album or playlist keep their existing behavior.

pullRequests.title: Fix a single-track Endless Mix looping over the same few songs

articles.title: Apple Home shows blinds moving in the right direction
articles.dek: Movements started by a wall switch or Home Assistant automation stop appearing reversed in the Home app.
body: A blind opening through a wall switch, scene or Home Assistant automation can appear to be closing in Apple Home. Home Assistant corrects the target position it reports while the blind moves, so Apple Home derives the right direction.
Partial positions requested in Apple Home remain intact, including when the blind arrives at its requested position. k.mifka makes their first contribution to Home Assistant Core with the fix.

articles.title: Music Assistant makes troubleshooting less of a slowdown
articles.dek: Turning on detailed logs no longer enables a costly second layer of debugging.
body: People asked to collect detailed Music Assistant logs should no longer make their server markedly slower in the process. Debug logging had also switched on Python’s event-loop debugging, which records a stack trace whenever work is scheduled.

Marcel van der Veldt separates the two settings. On the reported installation with 60 players, stack capture consumed 36 of every 60 CPU seconds and average event-loop delay reached 250 milliseconds with debug logging enabled. Developers retain the deeper checks through Python’s development mode.

articles.title: Music Assistant fixes clipped audio in its iOS app
articles.dek: Large audio blocks are split safely instead of losing their ending.
body: Music Assistant’s iOS app fixes clipped audio when a block of sound is too large for the native audio handoff. David Bishop splits blocks larger than 64 KB into pieces that fit, preserving the ending that previously went missing. The correction accompanies work on the app’s Sendspin audio connection.
